changes.title: Fed governor Waller muddies outlook on possible rate hike later this month
changes.summary: Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said Thursday that an inflation report next week will largely determine whether he supports an interest rate hike later this month or not.

changes.title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data
changes.summary: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, sounded optimistic about inflation’s trajectory but indicated he would support higher rates if progress does not continue.

changes.title: Benign Inflation Data Offers Reprieve to Fed as It Weighs Rate Increase
changes.summary: The latest Consumer Price Index report helped to reinforce the patient approach adopted by many officials at the Federal Reserve about raising rates, but it has not resolved the debate altogether.

changes.title: Inflation cooled last month as gas prices fell, though costs remain elevated
changes.summary: The modest decline could ease pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise their key interest rate to combat rising costs. Yet prices are still rising more quickly than average wages, underscoring the struggle many Americans have had with more expensive groceries, gas, and healthcare.

changes.title: Trump Restarts Battle to Fire Sitting Fed Governor Lisa Cook
changes.summary: The Trump administration, rebuffed by the Supreme Court in its first attempt to fire Lisa D. Cook, sent the Federal Reserve governor a letter saying it was “considering” removing her from the job.

changes.title: Weak Jobs Report Does Not Eliminate Prospects of Interest Rate Rise
changes.summary: Officials at the Federal Reserve are chiefly focused on the trajectory of inflation after five years of overshooting the central bank’s 2 percent target.

changes.title: Trump administration proceeds with efforts to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook
changes.summary: The Trump administration is moving ahead with its efforts to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, two months after the Supreme Court allowed her to retain her job while she fights the president's effort to terminate her over mortgage fraud allegations that she has denied.
